title: Edgecase: Regional cost curve — GPU-hour to $/1M tokens mapping
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet translates GPU-hour burn into $/1M tokens across regions for a set of representative serving configurations. It's an edge-case focused sensitivity analysis: short-sequence chat (16-64 tokens), long-context generation (2048+ tokens), and high-throughput embedding workloads. Aim is to expose non-linear regional behavior when utilization, preemptibility, and batching mix change.

Summary findings (top-line):
- Base $/1M tokens ranges from roughly $0.45 to $7.20 depending on region and model family under baseline assumptions.
- High-utilization (>=80%) improves $/1M by ~25-40% vs 40% utilization due to fixed-hour amortization and better batching.
- Preemptible/spot usage drops direct GPU-hour costs by ~40-60% but increases tail latency and retry overhead; effective $/1M savings depend on failure-handling tax (we model 10-30% extra token cost).
- APAC regions show 10-30% higher $/1M vs US when using reserved instances because of instance pricing and lower sustained utilization in our fleet mix.

Model inputs (editable):
- Model families modeled: small-chat (7B dense), med-chat (13B quantized), large-chat (70B fp16), embedder (2B dense).
- GPU types: A100-40GB (a100-40), A100-80GB (a100-80), H100-80GB (h100).
- Example baseline per-hour GPU list-price (after discounts):
  Region, a100-40 ($/hr), a100-80 ($/hr), h100 ($/hr)
  us-west-2, 3.25, 4.80, 7.10
  us-east-1, 3.20, 4.70, 6.95
  eu-west-1, 3.85, 5.10, 7.90
  ap-southeast-1, 4.10, 5.50, 8.40

Throughput assumptions (tokens/sec per GPU, avg prompt+completion token mix):
  Model, GPU type, tokens/sec (baseline), peak-batched-tokens/sec
  small-chat, a100-40, 1100, 1650
  med-chat, a100-80, 860, 1290
  large-chat, h100, 240, 360
  embedder, a100-40, 4500, 6750
Notes: baseline assumes typical request shapes and 1.5x KV cache hit for chat. Peak-batched assumes aggressive batching + continuous batching windows.

Utilization scenarios (percent of hour GPU is productive):
  Scenario, util%
  low, 30
  baseline, 55
  high, 80
  steady-batch, 95
We account for a 6% infra overhead (driver/OS/housekeeping) subtracted from raw util.

Simple conversion formula (applied per region/model/GPU):
  GPU_hour_tokens = tokens_per_sec * 3600 * effective_util
  $/1M_tokens = (GPU_hour_price / GPU_hour_tokens) * 1_000_000
  with effective_util = util% * (1 - infra_overhead) * batching_factor
  batching_factor = peak-batched / baseline throughput (capped at 1.8 in our model)
Example (us-west-2, med-chat on a100-80, baseline util=55%):
  tokens/sec = 860 -> GPU_hour_tokens = 860*3600*0.55*0.94*1.0 = ~1,606,248 tokens
  $/1M = (4.80 / 1,606,248) * 1e6 = $2.99 per 1M tokens

Sensitivity table samples (rounded):
  Region | Model | GPU | util | tokens/hr | $/1M tokens
  -----------------------------------------------------
  us-west-2 | small-chat | a100-40 | baseline(55%) | 6.75M | $0.48
  us-west-2 | med-chat | a100-80 | baseline(55%) | 3.6M | $1.33
  us-west-2 | large-chat | h100 | baseline(55%) | 0.48M | $14.79
  us-west-2 | embedder | a100-40 | baseline(55%) | 17.82M | $0.18

  eu-west-1 | med-chat | a100-80 | baseline(55%) | 3.6M | $1.42
  ap-southeast-1 | med-chat | a100-80 | baseline(55%) | 3.6M | $1.63

Edge cases highlighted:
- Long-context generation: for 8k-32k tokens per request, throughput drops but per-request overhead increases; when you amortize stop tokens the $/1M can look artificially low for very long single-shot generations but spikes on tail latencies and prefetch requirements. Run separate capacity lanes for >8k workloads.
- Low-util small models: small-chat on A100 when traffic is very spiky (util <25%) can cost >2x higher $/1M vs medium models colocated on larger GPUs with packing. Consider fractional-GPU tenancy or ML model-packing to reduce unit cost.
- Spot/Preemptible mixes: modeled effective price reductions and retry tax. If your retry tax >20%, spot savings can vanish for interactive features.

Operational playbook snippets:
- If observed $/1M for med-chat > modeled + 20%:
  1) Check per-server util and batch window percentiles (p50/p95).
  2) Verify KV cache hit rates and token-length distribution shifted up.
  3) Consider increasing batching window 10-25ms on low-latency routes with low p95.
  4) If region shows persistent >25% premium, shift lower-latency traffic to another region when legal/latency bounds allow.

Open questions / next iterations:
- Need empirical telemetry: run 1-week A/B with med-chat on a100-80 in eu-west-1 vs us-east-1 capturing tokens/sec per GPU and actual average token length per request.
- Model quantization impact: how does int4/in8 throughput map to our tokens/sec assumptions across model families? We flagged plus/minus 1.15x to 1.4x in throughput but need bench PRs.
- Autoscaling: what is the effective cold-start burn when scaling from 0 -> steady-batch for our Dedicated pools? Add a transient-cost line item.

Action items (owner tags):
- [Aisha] provision short bench runs (24h) for med-chat on a100-80 in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 (ticket INFRA-423).
- [Miguel] add quantization bench columns to the gsheet and start int8 runs (due 2025-02-10).
- [Liang] instrument token-length histogram pipeline on hosted-api routes to feed into model assumptions (due 2025-01-28).

Appendix: Quick reference numbers used in calculations (for reproducibility):
- infra_overhead = 0.06
- batching cap = 1.8x
- retry_tax_for_spot = 0.20 (scenario default)
- reserved_discount baseline applied to list price: 18% for US, 12% for EU, 5% for APAC (subject to procurement)

Notes on provenance:
This sheet synthesizes procurement price lists (internal pricing deck), recent fleet telemetry (last 90 days), and microbench results. It's intentionally chatty - meant to be a working artifact for the infrastructure and serving-runtime teams to iterate against.

If you want this exported to a formal capacity model, I can (Miguel/Aisha) produce a cleaned gsheet with scenario toggles (util %, batching factor, regional discounts) and a small python runner to produce regional cost curves (CSV) for the finance/business teams.

-- end of doc --
